subject: RFI: Evidence transport method + key rotation proof — proposed delivery
body:
--- Message 1/4 ---
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@crestbridge.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samuel Ortiz <s.ortiz@crestbridge.com>, Theresa Wong <t.wong@crestbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: evidence delivery options for large telemetry + KMS rotation proof

David —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the SIG. Two follow-ups from our security team as we start to assemble the audit packet: 1) For the key rotation proof you referenced, can you confirm the format and whether we can accept a CSV extract of rotation events or if we need full log bundles? 2) For large telemetry (10s of GB of token-level telemetry over a quarter) — what transport do you recommend for secure, auditable delivery? Our procurement needs ETA for artifacts and any temporary access constraints we should expect.

Also, please include any redaction guidance — we need to know what to expect before handing this to our auditors.

Appreciate it —
Lara Chen
Senior InfoSec Manager
Crestbridge Financial

--- Message 2/4 ---
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@crestbridge.com>
Cc: Samuel Ortiz <s.ortiz@crestbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: evidence delivery options for large telemetry + KMS rotation proof

Hi Lara —

Thanks — good questions. High-level answers up front, then a proposed delivery plan: 

1) Key rotation proof
- We can provide a CSV extract (sample attached) that enumerates rotation_id, key_id, previous_key_fingerprint, new_key_fingerprint, rotated_at (UTC), and performed_by (system/service account).
- For auditors that need full context, we can also deliver a gzipped log bundle containing the KMS audit records (Cloud KMS / HSM event stream format). This bundle contains the raw event payloads; we typically redact ephemeral identifiers per our redaction policy.

2) Large telemetry transfer
- Recommended: temporary cloud storage share + signed, time-limited access. For Crestbridge we can:
  a) Stage artifacts into an encrypted S3 bucket and provide pre-signed URLs (one-time download links) with expiration windows you choose (recommended 72 hours per package).
  b) Alternatively, use Azure Blob pre-signed SAS tokens if your auditors prefer Azure.
  c) For extremely large sets we can arrange an encrypted Gluster / rsync over SSH transfer window.

Redaction guidance
- Attached: redaction-guidelines-v1.pdf. We redact PII and full user prompt text by default; we keep token-level telemetry but replace user ids with consistent pseudonyms so auditors can trace sessions without seeing raw PII.

Proposed timeline & next steps
- 2026-12-17: I will circulate a manifest (names + sizes + intended expiry) and a sample CSV for key rotation (attached).
- 2026-12-20: Provide encrypted bundles staged to S3 with pre-signed links.
- If you require the raw bundles earlier or an alternative transport, let me know and I will route to the infra team for a short-term VPN/rsync window.

Attachments: sample-key-rotation-report-2026Q3.csv, redaction-guidelines-v1.pdf

Best,
David Kim
Head of Trust & Safety — Redwood Inference

--- Message 3/4 (internal) ---
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 08:53:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Crestbridge RFI — artifacts + redaction ask

Team —

Crestbridge (HB-4821) wants to schedule delivery next week. Key points:
- Provide CSV rotation extract + full gzipped KMS audit bundle as an option. The customer prefers CSV for speed but auditors may ask for raw logs.
- Telemetry set is ~38 GB compressed (Q3 token telemetry). We should stage in our audit-sprints bucket and produce pre-signed URLs with 72h TTL.
- They asked for clear redaction rules; attached a first draft. Can you review: Mina — confirm the pseudonymization approach is compliant with our data retention policy and that we are not leaking any full-prompt text. Jordan — can you handle staging and create the s3 manifest and short-lived URLs?

Security notes:
- Ensure server-side encryption (AES256) on the bucket and that object-level ACLs are disabled.
- For KMS raw bundles, double-check that HSM-signed attestations are included in the bundle metadata.

Deliverables I will send externally after your sign-off: manifest + s3-temp-access-manifest.txt, sample-key-rotation-report-2026Q3.csv, and the redaction guidance doc.

Thanks —
David

--- Message 4/4 ---
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@crestbridge.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Samuel Ortiz <s.ortiz@crestbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: evidence delivery options for large telemetry + KMS rotation proof

Lara —

Following up with our agreed delivery approach and links. Jordan and Mina have validated the exports and redactions. Summary below plus links.

What we are delivering
- Key rotation CSV (sample-key-rotation-report-2026Q3.csv) — contains rotation_id, key_id, old_fingerprint, new_fingerprint, rotated_at (UTC), initiated_by.
- Optional: KMS raw bundle (gzipped) — included in the manifest as an alternative for auditors who require raw events.
- Telemetry bundle (q3-token-telemetry-part-1.tar.gz, q3-token-telemetry-part-2.tar.gz) — split to keep file sizes manageable.
- Redaction guidance (redaction-guidelines-v1.pdf) and a short manifest (s3-temp-access-manifest.txt) that lists file names, sizes, and expiry window.

Access method & expiry
- All artifacts are staged to an encrypted S3 bucket. Pre-signed URLs are provided below with an initial 72-hour window from first access. We can extend on request but will default to the window for audit hygiene.
- For Doc delivery/contract reasons, we included a short additive agreement for temporary access; I’ve attached a DocuSign link to sign the addendum if procurement requires it.

Links & attachments
- Drive folder (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3CsecureShare
- DocuSign (temporary access addendum): https://www.docusign.com/secure/embeddedSigning/abc123
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/HB-4821

If your auditors want raw KMS logs delivered another way (VPN rsync or direct SCP), we can open a short maintenance window and provide host credentials. Please confirm preference and any PO/transport constraints by EOD Wednesday (2026-12-22) so Jordan can generate the presigned URLs and I can push the manifests.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

Best regards,
David Kim
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

--- End of thread ---
